description: TerraTwinn is an open-source web platform for identifying Earth analogs of Moon and Mars sites. Built with TypeScript and Next.js, it combines NASA planetary datasets (LOLA, HiRISE) with Earth observation data to evaluate terrain roughness, geology, and climate extremes. Our interactive decision engine ranks sites by balancing physical fidelity against mission logistics and cost. Open to collaborators skilled in planetary geology, geospatial data pipelines, and scientific data visualization!
summary:
TerraTwinn is a web platform that helps mission teams find the best places on Earth to test hardware bound for the Moon and Mars. Every rover, lander and habitat must be tested on Earth first, yet choosing a test site is still largely manual and based on experience. When terrain is misjudged, missions pay the price: in 2009, NASA’s Spirit rover became stuck in soft Martian soil and never drove again.

Users pick a target site on the Moon or Mars. TerraTwinn compares its terrain, geology and environmental conditions with Earth locations using NASA and global satellite data, then ranks the closest “twins” by an evidence score. Unlike pure similarity search, it also scores what engineers actually care about: mission type, distance to the nearest base, logistics and cost. Every ranking comes with charts and a factor breakdown, so teams can see, and defend, why a site ranks first.

Find the twin. Land the mission.

Github: https://github.com/SlimeQzz2606/TerraTwinn
details:
What it does / how it works

  1. Choose a target. The user selects a site on the Moon or Mars.
  2. Find Earth twins. TerraTwinn compares the target with Earth locations across terrain (slope, roughness), geology and surface material, and climate/environment, using NASA and global satellite datasets.
  3. Mission-aware scoring. Similarity is only part of the score. Each mission type weighs factors differently: a rover test prioritises slopes and soil, while a telescope or seismometer test also needs quiet ground, so seismic activity is added. Practical factors (distance from the nearest base, accessibility, logistics, estimated cost) are included.
  4. User-controlled weights. Users adjust how much each factor matters, and the ranking updates instantly.
  5. Transparent results. Each candidate site shows imagery, terrain data, charts and a factor-by-factor breakdown of its evidence score.

Benefits

  • Faster, data-driven test-site selection instead of manual research.
  • Lower cost: a near-perfect analog in an unreachable place can cost more than the test itself, so TerraTwinn balances fidelity against practicality.
  • Explainable, defensible decisions for reviews and proposals.
  • Accessible to small teams, universities and emerging space agencies without in-house field-geology expertise.

Intended impact
NASA’s Artemis program and China’s CLEP are both heading for the lunar south pole, and new rovers are being built for Mars. Each needs the right ground to test on first. TerraTwinn aims to make analog testing smarter and cheaper for flagship programs and low-budget teams alike, making space exploration more accessible to all.

Creativity

  • Reframes the question from “Where on Earth is similar?” to “Where should we actually test?” by combining scientific similarity with mission needs and real-world logistics.
  • Mission-aware, user-weighted scoring instead of one fixed similarity metric.
  • No black box: every score is explained.
  • Future work, Twin Drive: engineers enter a rover’s mass, speed range and centre of mass. A split screen then shows the same rover driving on the Earth analog and on Mars, where it weighs about 38% as much, revealing what Earth testing cannot capture. We plan to start with sites that have high-resolution HiRISE terrain models.

Factors we considered

  • Scientific fidelity: which surface properties matter most for each type of test.
  • Practicality: access, distance to infrastructure, logistics and cost.
  • Different needs per mission type (rover, lander, habitat, telescope/seismic instruments).
  • Transparency and trust: engineers must be able to justify site choices.
  • Data availability and resolution, which shapes our roadmap (e.g. starting Twin Drive where HiRISE models exist).
  • Accessibility for teams with limited budgets and expertise.
